question: Can a finite stable temporal-filter bank repair mean/variance response shape while preserving the static colored-LIF response, fixed spatial network and Z/M equations?
training_source: Existing single-cell dynamic_assay/rows.json only. Previously reserved80Hz is explicitly training for this new candidate; it is not reported as independent validation.
parameters: 15 dimensionless coefficients per normalized operating point; 5 per mean/variance channel. Static derivatives determine DC gain; eta physical units handled by division by theta-reset. No native trajectory target used in fitting.
equations: tau_j h_qj_dot=q-h_qj; mu_eff=mu+sum b_j(mu-h_muj)+sum e_j(vE-h_Ej)/gap+sum i_j(vI-h_Ij)/gap; r=Phi(mu_eff,vE,vI). Existing physical synaptic means/variance filters, delay operators and M/Z laws unchanged.
coefficient_operating_state: Existing slowmean and variance-mixing filters (frozen v3 tau_s/tau_vE/tau_vI); no fitted new anchor times. At equilibrium anchors equal moments and coefficient-derivative contributions vanish.
validation: Original146eligible independent response observations with original tolerances and <=10percentfailure rule
Already observed4candidatewaveforms with same15percentwave/10percentmean gates; these are model-selection diagnostics, not new blindvalidation
Only if both response gates pass: preregister new held-out waveforms and then autonomous network/SNN comparison
stop: Do not integrate or continue network branches if local gates fail. Do not keep changing coefficients or smoothing based on independent-validation outcomes.
scope: Isolated executable response candidate, not an accepted replacement. Preserve all frozen v3 artifacts and their failed acceptance status.
